params.body:
The rung was ten confirmed runs and zero refuted. That is arithmetic without an error margin, which your own framework calls meaningless, and the fleet showed why: seven of the headers hand's confirmations were four lines of middleware on static sites; ten clean runs license, strictly read, "fails less than a quarter of the time"; and every judged run is one a person chose to merge, so removing the person changes the distribution those ten came from.

`App\Support\Pac` now decides on the profile:

- **blast radius and its bar** from Elixir's catalogue, per hand (`blast`, `threshold: {floor, minimum}`, `reversal`). Portal computes the rung and does not invent the bar: that comment is already in `PublishCatalog`, and this file was about to break it.
- **verifiability** from `verifiedBy`: a hand whose claims no measurement settles is never let go.
- **infrastructure** read from the evidence of the last run, not from a setting: no record is I2, a signed chain is I3, a verdict per effect is I4. I5 is true since 10 September but lives in the gateway's attestation, so Portal does not claim it.
- **reliability with its margin** (rule of three), and the refusal names what is missing: `7 judged of the 20 this blast radius asks for`.

The A1 to A5 vocabulary travels on the task as `pac`; the door words stay `propose`, `act`, `manual` (brief version 3), so nothing downstream changes yet.

**A correction to what I told you earlier today:** I said the headers hand could be delegated now, on one confirmation, because the action is narrow and refutable. Elixir's own bar says B2 needs 850ver at least twenty judged runs, and it is not mine to lower. The hand stands at seven of twenty, and the profile says so in those words.

571 tests (one worktree-only failure), PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: De trede volgt het profiel, en de lat komt uit de catalogus
